Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

actimetrics 0.10.0

Internal

  • Imports actiread with except = "tzoffset_to_tz", so actibase can export tzoffset_to_tz() later without an import conflict.
  • GGIR is no longer listed in Suggests; it was not used.
  • Checks for agcounts and stepcount now use requireNamespace(pkg, partial = TRUE) instead of rlang::check_installed()/rlang::is_installed(), so their .onLoad hooks (which initialize Python via reticulate) do not run during the check. This fixes the CRAN NOTE in “checking dependencies in R code”.

New features

  • New sleep-period-time guiders following the GGIR sleep definitions (implemented without calling GGIR): acti_sleep_hdcza(), acti_sleep_hlrb(), acti_sleep_horangle(), acti_sleep_l5(), acti_sleep_notworn(), acti_sleep_setwindow(), and acti_sleep_diary(), dispatched by acti_sleep_guider() (see acti_sleep_guider_requirements()). acti_sleep_sib() detects sustained inactivity bouts, acti_sleep_label() and acti_sleep_labels() turn guiders into epoch-level sleep/wake labels, acti_sleep_fuse_labels() combines labels with STAPLE, and acti_sleep_ensemble() runs the whole pipeline from raw or epoch data.
  • New activity-intensity classifiers: acti_threshold_counts() and acti_threshold_enmo() for user-supplied cut-points, and published cut-points in acti_threshold_montoye(), acti_threshold_sasaki(), acti_threshold_romanzini(), and acti_threshold_hildebrand() (with acti_threshold_hildebrand_wrist() and acti_threshold_hildebrand_hip()).
  • New acti_calculate_wear_raw() estimates non-wear from raw tri-axial acceleration, implemented without calling GGIR or actipy. Like acti_calculate_wear(), it takes a method argument and passes ... to the method function:
    • acti_calculate_wear_raw_ggir() (method = "ggir", default): the GGIR non-wear and clipping algorithm (van Hees et al. 2011, 2013), exposing GGIR’s settings: the medium/long window sizes, the "2023" and "2013" approaches, the standard-deviation and range thresholds, the clipping threshold or dynamic range, edge correction, and the night-time short non-wear filter.
    • acti_calculate_wear_raw_actipy() (method = "actipy"): stationary episodes of Doherty et al. (2017), as in actipy’s detect_nonwear(), with the window, patience, and standard-deviation threshold exposed.
    acti_calculate_wear() remains the count-based (Choi/Troiano) method.

Bug fixes and other changes

  • acti_process() frees the raw data once counts are calculated, before non-wear detection and day inclusion.

  • acti_calculate_stepcount() (and py_acti_calculate_stepcount()) now return times in the input’s time zone. stepcount reports local clock times without a time zone, which were previously labelled UTC, shifting steps by the input’s UTC offset (e.g. one hour for British Summer Time). A new tz argument sets the time zone, which is needed for file input (default "UTC").

  • epoch/unit arguments are standardized with actibase::acti_standardize_epoch(), so acti_calculate_counts() accepts epoch = "1 min" and the measure functions accept numeric seconds or strings such as "30s". ensure_all_time = TRUE no longer errors for units such as "5 seconds" or "1 minute", and acti_calculate_mims() no longer errors for units without a space such as "1min".

  • acti_calculate_ai() and acti_calculate_mad() now default to verbose = TRUE.

  • acti_apply_cole_kripke(), acti_apply_sadeh(), and acti_apply_tudor_locke() no longer add a superfluous vector.magnitude column (a copy of counts) to their output.

  • acti_apply_cole_kripke() and acti_apply_sadeh() no longer return the count column that actigraph.sleepr uses internally for scoring (axis1 truncated and, for Cole-Kripke, divided by 100). It overwrote any count column in the input, which is now kept.

actimetrics 0.9.0

CRAN release: 2026-10-20

  • Works with both actibase 0.6.0 and 0.8.0: acti_calculate_measures() uses acti_flag_qc_all() when actibase provides it and flag_qc_all() otherwise, since actibase 0.8.0 renames it.

Breaking changes

  • acti_process() and acti_process_study() now aim to match ActiLife for GT3X data: files are read with digits = 8 (unless digits is given), resampled to 30Hz, then rounded to 3 digits half away from zero, as ActiLife does. Previously the data were read at 5 digits and not rounded, giving counts that differed from ActiLife by 1-3 in many epochs. Rounding 5-digit data is not a fix: it rounds twice and differs from ActiLife more often. Counts from GT3X files will change slightly.

New features

  • acti_calculate_counts() and acti_process() gain round_digits to round X/Y/Z half away from zero (base round() rounds 0.0625 to 0.062) after resampling and before counting. In acti_process(), the default NULL uses 3 for GT3X data and no rounding otherwise; NA turns it off.

actimetrics 0.8.0

Breaking changes

  • acti_apply_cole_kripke(), acti_apply_sadeh(), and acti_calculate_wear(use_magnitude = FALSE) now error if axis1 is missing. Both sleep algorithms score the vertical axis, so vector-magnitude counts are no longer silently converted with axis1 = VM / sqrt(3).
  • acti_calculate_wear() errors with an informative message unless the data are 60-second epochs (required by Choi and Troiano).
  • Step summaries (acti_calculate_stepcount(), acti_calculate_verisense(), acti_calculate_forest(), acti_calculate_sdt()) now return NA for epochs where all values are missing (e.g. non-wear) rather than 0 steps; walking from acti_calculate_stepcount() is likewise NA.
  • With allow_truncation = TRUE, acti_calculate_auc() and acti_calculate_fast_mims() mark an epoch with any out-of-range axis as -0.01 (all axes and the total), as MIMSunit does, rather than adding the -1 sentinel into the total.

New features

  • New acti_process_study() processes every supported raw file (GT3X, CWA, GENEActiv BIN, CSV) in a directory with acti_process() and saves RDS files. Failures are always reported with a warning and listed in the failed attribute of the result. CSV files are read with readr, which is now in Imports.
  • acti_apply_tudor_locke() gains sleep_col to use a sleep-state column with another name (e.g. from acti_apply_tudor_locke_diary()).
  • acti_calculate_ai() has its own documentation page describing the (noise-unadjusted) Activity Index of Bai et al. (2016).

Bug fixes

  • acti_calculate_counts() subsets to time/X/Y/Z before calling agcounts, whose start-of-record padding failed on data with extra columns (e.g. GENEActiv light/temperature).
  • The first-second padding before agcounts keeps all columns, attributes, and the timezone, builds the padded times on an exact sample grid, and no longer re-prefixes the existing transformation history. It is kept by default alongside the upstream fix (bhelsel/agcounts#51), as it also avoids agcounts’ duplicate zero-count rows and works with older agcounts.
  • acti_calculate_wear() now passes ... to actigraph.sleepr (arguments such as min_period_len were ignored) and is not affected by existing wear columns.
  • mims_default_extrapolation(), mims_default_interpolation(), and mims_default_filtering() now record their transformations.
  • acti_calculate_ai() skips 1-second windows with a single sample instead of making the whole epoch NA, and warns for data sampled under 2 Hz.
  • acti_calculate_verisense() validates method with match.arg(), so the default is "original".
  • acti_calculate_fast_mims() uses the sample rate of the processed (100 Hz) data; a supplied sample_rate is ignored with a warning.
  • A user-supplied sample_rate in acti_calculate_measures() is now passed through to the activity-count calculation, and a missing sample rate gives an informative error from acti_calculate_counts(resample = FALSE).
  • Epoch/unit strings such as "30s" and "1min" are parsed with lubridate, consistent with lubridate::floor_date().
  • py_acti_calculate_stepcount() and py_acti_calculate_forest() return their result visibly.
  • Fixed the aggregated_at_ transformation label and documentation of verbose and lfe_select.

actimetrics 0.7.0

  • Add sleep diary labeling for Tudor–Locke and adapt diary labels for actigraph.sleepr::apply_tudor_locke().

  • Declare actigraph.sleepr as an installation dependency for sleep wrappers.

  • Fixing bug with acti_calculate_mims due to not subsetting XYZ.

actimetrics 0.5.0

  • Removing count from globalVariables.

actimetrics 0.4.0

CRAN release: 2026-09-17

actimetrics 0.3.0
